::: {.tldr}
The graph **pauses before the agent acts**. A person can inspect the state, approve the action, change it, or rewind to any earlier step and branch off. All of this relies on the checkpointer from the previous lesson.
:::

## The flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S([START]) --> L[llm]
  L -- tool calls --> H{{"⏸ pause<br/>interrupt_before"}}
  H -- "approve: stream(None)" --> A[action]
  H -. "edit: update_state" .-> H
  L -- no tool --> E([END])
  A --> L
```

## Pausing before a node

```python
self.graph = graph.compile(
    checkpointer=checkpointer,
    interrupt_before=["action"],     # stop before any tool runs
)
```

## Key ideas

::: {.concepts}
::: {.concept}
`get_state(thread)`

The current state. `.next` shows the node that will run next, e.g. `('action',)`. Empty means finished.
:::
::: {.concept}
`stream(None, thread)`

`None` as input means "continue from where you stopped".
:::
::: {.concept}
`update_state(thread, values)`

Change the state, e.g. edit a tool call. Creates a new snapshot.
:::
::: {.concept}
`get_state_history(thread)`

Every snapshot, newest first. Resume from any of them: time travel.
:::
::: {.concept}
`as_node="action"`

Write an update as if that node produced it, e.g. inject a fake tool result.
:::
:::

## Approving an action

```python
thread = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
for event in abot.graph.stream({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="Weather in SF?")]}, thread):
    print(event)

print(abot.graph.get_state(thread).next)   # ('action',): waiting for approval

for event in abot.graph.stream(None, thread):   # approve: run the tool and continue
    print(event)
```

## A reducer that can replace messages

`operator.add` always appends. To **edit** a message, use a reducer that replaces messages with the same `id`:

```python
from uuid import uuid4

def reduce_messages(left: list[AnyMessage], right: list[AnyMessage]) -> list[AnyMessage]:
    for message in right:
        if not message.id:
            message.id = str(uuid4())
    merged = left.copy()
    for message in right:
        for i, existing in enumerate(merged):
            if existing.id == message.id:
                merged[i] = message        # same id: replace
                break
        else:
            merged.append(message)         # new id: append
    return merged

class AgentState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], reduce_messages]
```

## Editing an action before it runs

```python
current = abot.graph.get_state(thread)
last = current.values["messages"][-1]
last.tool_calls = [{
    "name": tool.name,                                  # use the tool's real name
    "args": {"query": "current weather in Louisiana"},
    "id": last.tool_calls[0]["id"],                     # same id
}]
abot.graph.update_state(thread, current.values)         # same message id → replaced

for event in abot.graph.stream(None, thread):           # runs the edited search
    print(event)
```

## Time travel

```python
states = list(abot.graph.get_state_history(thread))   # newest first
to_replay = states[-3]                                 # an earlier snapshot

for event in abot.graph.stream(None, to_replay.config):   # resume from there
    print(event)
```

Editing an old snapshot and resuming from it creates a **new branch**. The original history is kept.

## Injecting a tool result

Skip the real tool and give the model a result yourself:

```python
from langchain_core.messages import ToolMessage

state = abot.graph.get_state(thread)
call_id = state.values["messages"][-1].tool_calls[0]["id"]
fake = ToolMessage(tool_call_id=call_id, name=tool.name, content="54 degrees and sunny")

abot.graph.update_state(thread, {"messages": [fake]}, as_node="action")
for event in abot.graph.stream(None, thread):    # goes straight to the llm node
    print(event)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Remember
- `interrupt_before` = a checkpoint where a person can approve.
- Resume with `stream(None, thread)`.
- `update_state` never erases history: every change is a new snapshot.
- Keep the same `id` to **replace** a message (needs a replacing reducer).
- `as_node` decides which node the update counts as, and so what runs next.
- The agent resumes from the **saved state**, not from your code. Change the state, not only the variables.
:::

## Quiz

<details class="quiz">
<summary>What does <code>get_state(thread).next == ()</code> mean?</summary>
<p>Nothing is left to run: the agent has finished.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>You edit an old snapshot and resume from it. Is the original history lost?</summary>
<p>No. It creates a new branch, and the original snapshots stay in the history.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Why use <code>as_node="action"</code> when injecting a fake tool result?</summary>
<p>So the graph treats the update as the output of the action node. The next step is then the llm node, and the real tool never runs.</p>
</details>
